summary: Audit of capability gating for the seven W1 platform-settings screens (apps/web/src/features/platform-settings/) and the R1 release screens (apps/web/src/features/r1/R1Screens.tsx), plus related authorization screens. The web shell gates routes via capabilitiesForRoute(route) and isRouteVisible(route, capabilities); per-control visibility on mutation buttons is decided server-side by the allowed_actions payload projected through actionCapability in PlatformSettingsMockData.ts. The route map (apps/web/src/shell/routes.ts) is the only client-side capability gate; every screen below is reached through that gate.

context.gating_mechanism: routes.ts capabilitiesForRoute -> isRouteVisible (any-of) -> RouteAccessGuard / PlatformSettingsLayout.canOpenSection; per-control visibility on platform-settings is isAllowed(allowedActions, action) projected through PlatformSettingsMockData.actionCapability (server-driven). R1 screens have no per-control gate; they rely on the route gate alone.

issues: Route gate is an any-of of five read-only capabilities (PLATFORM_SETTINGS_OVERVIEW_CAPABILITIES = platform_settings.read, platform_settings.calendar.read, platform_operations.backup.read, platform_operations.health.read, platform_operations.maintenance.manage). A principal holding only platform_settings.read (or any other single read) reaches an overview screen that exposes the runBackup mutation button (isAllowed(allowedActions, 'platform_operations.backup.run') lines 165, 245). Read-only routes must not funnel principals into a mutation-bearing dashboard.

The overview umbrella mixes platform_settings.read with platform_operations.maintenance.manage (a mutation capability) — using a mutation capability as a route-gate passkey while the screen advertises runBackup is a confusion between read gate and mutation gate.

Route gate (routes.ts line 421) advertises only platform_settings.read, but SecuritySettingsScreen gates the createDraft, setValue, validate and publish actions on platform_settings.manage / platform_settings.publish (lines 61-62). Both are absent from the route map. Per-control gate (isAllowed) is server-driven via allowed_actions, so the read-only route gate hides nothing — principals with only platform_settings.read see controls that vanish only because the server declined to include manage/publish in allowed_actions.

Route gate uses platform_settings.calendar.read; canCreate is decided only by token presence (line 101: const canCreate = token !== undefined) — no capability check. Anyone whose principal context exposes the calendars screen can call createBusinessCalendar with createPlatformSettingsDraft-equivalent surface, then publishBusinessCalendar / setBusinessCalendarException / setBusinessCalendarWeekday. The required platform_settings.calendar.manage / .publish capabilities are never consulted at the client.

canPublish checks platform_settings.calendar.publish or platform_settings.publish (line 102) but those are NOT in the route gate; a principal admitted by the read gate will render the publish button unconditionally and rely on the server's allowed_actions to suppress it.

Route gate is platform_operations.backup.read but BackupsScreen exposes three mutation controls (canRun = platform_operations.backup.run, canRequest = platform_operations.restore.request, canConfirm = platform_operations.restore.confirm; lines 79-90). The first two capabilities are absent from the route gate; restore.confirm is also missing from the actionCapability map in PlatformSettingsMockData (lines 101-115), so it will never be projected by allowed_actions even when the server emits it.
Read-route / mutation-screen mismatch: route entries 79-90 advertise three mutation actions while routes.ts line 425 admits the screen with a single read capability.

Route gate is platform_operations.logs.read (DEFERRED_CAPABILITIES, so the route is hidden — navigation/UI never exposes it). TechnicalLogsScreen nonetheless exposes a platform_operations.logs.restore mutation button (line 194). Even if a future release un-defers logs, the restore control would render to anyone with the read capability — no client-side check distinguishes read from restore.
DEFERRED_CAPABILITIES strips the route but the screen still imports the mutation action; an audit-only principal can never trigger it, but the screen contract is inconsistent with the route gate.

Route gate (platform_operations.health.read) is read-only; PlatformHealthScreen gates both edit-policy and review-routing-policies buttons on platform_operations.alerts.manage (lines 283, 292). A principal admitted to the health screen by read-only capability renders the edit button; the screen relies on the server's allowed_actions to hide it — no client-side capability fallback.

Route gate (routes.ts line 430) requires platform_operations.maintenance.manage OR platform_operations.maintenance.cancel, but the schedule-window action (canSchedule, line 47) requires only platform_operations.maintenance.manage — a cancel-only principal admitted by the OR shortcut cannot actually run schedulePlatformMaintenanceWindow, yet no client-side gate excludes them. Conversely, a manage-only principal who lacks cancel still passes the route gate and the canCancel button is suppressed only via allowed_actions. Either side can be admitted by the route with the wrong per-action capability set.
Admit policy (PlatformSettingsMockData.ts lines 156-159) hardcodes the cancel bypass but not its inverse; schedule-only delegation has no symmetric path.

Route gate is tasks.read + tasks.list (routes.ts lines 408-409). TasksScreen exposes complete / return-completion actions via transitionTask (lines 299-303, 257). The required capability is tasks.complete (CapabilityCatalog.php line 39), which is not in the route gate and not checked anywhere in the component. A principal admitted only by tasks.read renders the mutation controls; suppression relies on the server's 403.

Route gate is work_definition.read + work_definition.list. WorkDefinitionsScreen (lines 368-393) calls createWorkDefinition, createWorkDefinitionVersion and publishWorkDefinitionVersion. None of work_definition.create / work_definition.publish is in the route gate. Form (lines 398-409) is rendered unconditionally once the principal is admitted; the publish relies on the server to refuse it.

Route gate any-of allows workflow.read OR workflow.list OR workflow.manage (routes.ts line 392). WorkflowAdminScreen (lines 448-468) calls createWorkflowDefinition and publishWorkflowVersion. workflow.read / .list are read-only; admitting by them surfaces a screen whose primary action is publishWorkflowVersion. Only workflow.manage should be in the route gate.

Route gate is null (routes.ts line 344: case 'search' returns null) — any authenticated principal can reach the search form. The copy says 'The server returns authorized results only' (line 561), which is a server-trust signal only; the screen itself exposes no capability filter. Authorization gaps are not surfaced to the user until the API responds.

Route gate is reporting.list (routes.ts line 411); ReportsScreen renders an export-report Button (line 768) calling requestReportExport / createReportExport unconditionally. The required capability is reporting.export (CapabilityCatalog.php line 61), absent from the route gate. A principal admitted by reporting.list only sees an active export button that the server is expected to refuse.

Route gate is reporting.dashboard (routes.ts line 413) and the screen is read-only — control field is correctly 'read'. No defects to record, but listed for cross-reference with the workspace-routes logic in AppWorkspaceShell.tsx (canViewDashboards = principal.capabilities?.includes('reporting.dashboard') === true).

Route gate is authorization.role.read AND authorization.capability.read (routes.ts line 369). The screen correctly consumes both — but the gate forces a principal with only authorization.role.read to navigate into a screen whose workspace-tabs list also requires authorization.capability.read (lines 36-37 of the workspace). Result: principals with only role.read see the Roles tab but the Capabilities tab is silently absent (the screen handles this with visibleResources, not with a route-level capability gate).

Route gate is authorization.assignment.read. AuthorizationAdmin renders AdminForm for resource === 'role-assignments' (line 307), which calls createRoleAssignment (line 178). The form is rendered unconditionally when the screen is reached. There is no client-side gate for the actual mutation capability (authorization.assignment.manage, line 50 of CapabilityCatalog.php).

Route gate is authorization.delegation.read. AdminForm renders for resource === 'delegations' (line 307) and calls createDelegation (line 179). Required mutation capability is authorization.delegation.manage (CapabilityCatalog.php). No per-control client-side gate.

Route gate any-of authorization.policy.read (routes.ts lines 378-380). Screen is read-only (matrix view). No mutation controls surfaced; per resource the screen does not render AdminForm for policy resources (line 307 guards role-assignments and delegations only).
Same route-gate classification as classification-policies. Screen is read-only; no per-control gate required.
Route gate is authorization.capability.read (routes.ts line 371). Read-only listing; no defects to record.

Route gate any-of organization.facility.read + organization.unit.read (routes.ts line 355). Workspace hosts the structure tab which renders mutation controls via OrganizationDrawers (FacilityDrawer, ClusterDrawer, PersonDrawer, AddPositionDrawer, EndAssignmentDrawer). The drawer mutations require organization.unit.manage / organization.person.manage; neither is in the route gate. Suppression depends on each drawer consuming its own capability (C-008/C-009/C-010 area per the closure register).

Route gate is organization.unit.read. Screen renders AddUnitDrawer / AddPositionDrawer mutations; client-side gate for organization.unit.manage is delegated to drawer adapters (C-009). No per-control gate in the screen itself.

Route gate is organization.person.read. Screen exposes AssignmentDrawer + ClusterDrawer + PersonDrawer mutations; client-side gate for organization.person.manage is delegated to drawer adapters (C-010 area).

Route gate is organization.temporary-assignment.read. Screen exposes EndAssignmentDrawer and AddPositionDrawer mutations; mutation capability organization.temporary-assignment.manage is not in the route gate.

Route gate is organization.import.read. ImportReview is read/inspect-focused — review of an import job — and does not surface mutation controls to the principal (the mutation is performed by the import job runner). Listed for completeness: gate is correctly read-only.
Route gate is identity.account.read. Screen exposes a search/list projection; mutation capability identity.account.manage is not surfaced as a client gate (the route is the only gate).
Route gate is workflow.approve + work_definition.publish (routes.ts line 396). Screen exposes approve / return / escalate mutation controls; gate is correctly scoped to the mutation capability set.
Route gate is workflow.author. Screen is the procedure authoring surface (create/publish); gate matches the mutation set.
Route gate is workflow.author; screen submits a request — appropriate for an authoring capability.

Route gate any-of workflow.decide + workflow.reassign + workflow.escalate (routes.ts lines 401-402). Screen exposes decide / reassign / escalate mutation controls; gate matches. Note: a principal holding only workflow.decide renders the inbox but not the reassign controls.
Route gate same as /approvals. Detail exposes mutation controls; gating consistent.
Route gate is workflow.read + workflow.list (routes.ts line 404). Screen is read-only (my requests list); gate matches.
Route gate is workflow.read + workflow.list. Detail exposes status + history; no mutation controls.

Route gate is authorization.audit.read. Screen is the coverage dashboard; read-only. Note: the same capability is shared with /api-docs which is a developer surface — funneling principals to coverage by audit.read is the intended shape.
Route gate is authorization.audit.read (shared with /coverage). Listed for completeness — read-only gate is appropriate.
Route gate is authorization.decision.read. Screen is read-only (decision explanation); gate matches.

Route gate is organization.unit.read (routes.ts line 375). Screen shows the supervisory surface inside AuthorizationAdmin; AdminForm is NOT rendered for supervisory (line 307 guards only role-assignments / delegations). Read-only. Note: the gate uses organization.unit.read which is unrelated to the supervisory surface — gate is leaky.
